sa13:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa13:2.1: It was then that the Bhagavān addressed the monks,
sa13:2.2: “If sentient beings didn’t enjoy form, then they wouldn’t be affected by it.
sa13:2.3: It’s because they do enjoy form that sentient beings are affected and attached to it.
sa13:2.4: Thus, when sentient beings don’t enjoy feeling … conception … volition … awareness, they aren’t affected by it.
sa13:2.5: It’s because sentient beings do enjoy feeling … conception … volition … awareness that they are affected and attached to it.
sa13:3.1: “Monks, if form weren’t trouble for sentient beings, then sentient beings wouldn’t become disillusioned with it.
sa13:3.2: It’s because form is trouble for sentient beings that they do become disillusioned with it.
sa13:3.3: Thus, if feeling … conception … volition … awareness wasn’t trouble for sentient beings, they wouldn’t become disillusioned with it.
sa13:3.4: It’s because feeling … perception … volition … awareness is trouble for sentient beings that they do become disillusioned with it.
sa13:4.1: “Monks, if sentient beings had no escape from form, then sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.
sa13:4.2: It’s because sentient beings have an escape from form that they do escape from it.
sa13:4.3: Thus, if sentient beings had no escape from feeling … conception … volition … awareness, they wouldn’t escape from it.
sa13:4.4: It’s because sentient beings have an escape from feeling … conception … volition … awareness that they do escape from it.
sa13:5.1: “Monks, if I didn’t truly know the enjoyment of the five acquired aggregates to be enjoyment … trouble to be trouble … escape to be escape, I wouldn’t be freed, escaped, and parted with them.
sa13:5.2: I would have forever stood in delusion among gods like Māra or Brahmā,  ascetics and priests, or the assemblies of gods and humans, and I couldn’t have realized my attainment of the unsurpassed and complete awakening.
sa13:6.1: “Monks, it’s because I truly knew the enjoyment of the five acquired aggregates to be enjoyment … trouble to be trouble … escape to be escape that I was freed, escaped, parted, and liberated from bondage.
sa13:6.2: I never again stood in delusion among gods like Māra or Brahmā, ascetics and priests, or the assemblies of gods and humans, and I could realize my attainment of the unsurpassed and complete awakening.”
sa13:7.1: When the monks heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and approved.
